s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, cutaneous vascular lesions with erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
salient_findings: Multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
Firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders
Thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles
key_facts: Female patient in her late 20s
2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions located on left upper arm, left axilla, and lateral thoracic region
No triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma occurred before lesion appearance
No fever, weight loss, or fatigue
No extracutaneous involvement observed
Histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels
Endothelial cells were plump but displayed no significant cytologic atypia
Immunohistochemistry results positive for CD31, CD34, Ki-67 (<1%)
Immunohistochemistry results negative for podoplanin (D2-40) and human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

shortlist.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, and histopathological findings of irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels

shortlist.label: Tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the patient's symptoms and histopathological results, including the presence of plump endothelial cells and positive immunohistochemistry for CD31 and CD34

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similarities with the patient's clinical presentation and histopathological findings, including the presence of irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels

shortlist.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the patient's symptoms and histopathological results, including the presence of plump endothelial cells and positive immunohistochemistry for CD31 and CD34

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and histopathological findings are consistent with this diagnosis, including the presence of erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques with irregular borders, along with the histopathological findings of irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels and plump endothelial cells, is consistent with Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma. The immunohistochemistry results, including positivity for CD31 and CD34, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Tufted angioma
rejected.why: While tufted angioma can present with similar skin lesions, the histopathological findings in this case, such as the irregularly branched blood vessels, are more characteristic of Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.

rejected.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Retiform hemangioendothelioma typically presents with a more distinctive retiform pattern of blood vessels, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
rejected.why: Spindle cell hemangioma is characterized by a distinct spindle cell morphology, which is not mentioned in the histopathological findings of this case.

rejected.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
rejected.why: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma typically presents with a targetoid appearance and hemosiderin deposition, which is not described in this case.
